description: Arrays of objects encoding – list form for non-uniform objects and complex structures

tests.name: uses list form for objects with different fields
tests.expected:
items[2]:
  - id: 1
    name: First
  - id: 2
    name: Second
    extra: true

tests.name: uses list form for objects with nested values
tests.expected:
items[2]:
  - id: 1
    nested:
      x: 1
  - id: 2
    nested:
      y: 2
tests.note: The nested column mixes key sets {x} and {y}, so it is not nested-uniform (§9.3), so the array uses list form

tests.name: preserves field order in list items - array first
preserves field order in list items - primitive first
uses list form for objects containing arrays of arrays
uses tabular form for nested uniform object arrays
tests.note: Tabular header on hyphen line with rows at depth +2 and sibling fields at depth +1

tests.name: uses list form for nested object arrays with mismatched keys
tests.expected:
items[1]:
  - users[2]:
      - id: 1
        name: Ada
      - id: 2
    status: active

tests.name: uses list form for objects with multiple array fields
tests.expected:
items[1]:
  - nums[2]: 1,2
    tags[2]: a,b
    name: test

tests.name: uses list form for objects with only array fields
encodes objects with empty arrays in list form
uses canonical encoding for multi-field list-item objects with tabular arrays
tests.note: Tabular header on hyphen line with rows at depth +2 and sibling fields at depth +1

tests.name: uses canonical encoding for single-field list-item tabular arrays
tests.note: Tabular header on hyphen line with rows at depth +2

tests.name: places empty arrays on hyphen line when first
encodes empty object list items as bare hyphen
tests.note: Empty object list items encode as a single "-" line at the list-item depth

tests.name: uses field order from first object for tabular headers
uses list form when one object has nested field
tests.expected:
items[2]:
  - id: 1
    data: string
  - id: 2
    data:
      nested: true

tests.name: uses list form for arrays containing empty objects
tests.note: Empty objects are excluded from tabular detection (§9.3), so the array uses list form with bare hyphen markers (§10)

tests.name: encodes a keyed-eligible object in a tabular column as a nested field group
tests.note: Keyed tabular form is mandated in object-field and root positions, not in a column
